name: Alexanderplatz
short_description: Alexanderplatz is a large public square and transport hub in the former East Berlin, named after the Russian Tsar Alexander I.

name: World Clock (Weltzeituhr)
short_description: The World Clock (Weltzeituhr) on Alexanderplatz was built in 1969 and shows the time in cities around the world.

name: Red City Hall (Rotes Rathaus)
short_description: The Red City Hall (Rotes Rathaus) is the seat of Berlin's Governing Mayor and Senate, named after its red brick façade.

name: TV Tower (Fernsehturm)
short_description: The TV Tower (Fernsehturm) is 368 metres tall, the tallest structure in Germany, built by the GDR in 1969, with a viewing platform and a revolving restaurant.

name: Nikolai Quarter (Nikolaiviertel)
short_description: The Nikolai Quarter (Nikolaiviertel) is Berlin's oldest residential area, around the Nikolai Church, rebuilt by the GDR in the 1980s for the city's 750th anniversary.

name: Humboldt Forum
short_description: The Humboldt Forum is a museum and cultural centre inside the reconstructed Berlin Palace, opened in 2021.

name: Berlin Cathedral (Berliner Dom)
short_description: Berlin Cathedral (Berliner Dom) is the largest Protestant church in Berlin, completed in 1905, with a dome that visitors can climb for views of the city.

name: Museum Island (Museumsinsel)
short_description: Museum Island (Museumsinsel) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the Spree river with five major museums, including the Neues Museum, home of the bust of Nefertiti.

name: Neue Wache
short_description: The Neue Wache is a neoclassical building by Karl Friedrich Schinkel and today Germany's central memorial to the victims of war and dictatorship, with the sculpture 'Mother with her Dead Son' by Käthe Kollwitz.

name: Bebelplatz
short_description: Bebelplatz is the square where the Nazis burned books in 1933; an underground memorial shows empty bookshelves.

name: Gendarmenmarkt
short_description: Gendarmenmarkt is often called Berlin's most beautiful square, with the Konzerthaus between the French and the German Cathedral.

name: Checkpoint Charlie
short_description: Checkpoint Charlie was the most famous border crossing between East and West Berlin during the Cold War, where US and Soviet tanks faced each other in October 1961.

name: Topography of Terror (Topographie des Terrors)
short_description: The Topography of Terror is a free documentation centre about the crimes of the Nazi regime, on the site of the former Gestapo and SS headquarters.

name: Potsdamer Platz
short_description: Potsdamer Platz was a no-man's-land next to the Berlin Wall and was rebuilt after reunification with modern office towers.

name: Site of Hitler's Bunker (Führerbunker)
short_description: The site of Hitler's Bunker (Führerbunker) is where Hitler's underground bunker was located and where he died in 1945; today it is a car park with an information board.

name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe (Holocaust Memorial)
short_description: The Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe (Holocaust Memorial) opened in 2005 and has 2,711 concrete slabs and an information centre underneath.

name: Tiergarten
short_description: Tiergarten is one of Berlin's largest parks, a former royal hunting ground in the city centre.

name: Reichstag
short_description: The Reichstag is the seat of the German parliament (Bundestag); visitors can go up to its glass dome for free with advance registration.

name: Brandenburg Gate (Brandenburger Tor)
short_description: The Brandenburg Gate (Brandenburger Tor) was built in 1791 and is Berlin's most famous landmark and a symbol of the division and reunification of Germany.

name: Victory Column (Siegessäule)
short_description: The Victory Column (Siegessäule) in the Tiergarten celebrates Prussian military victories, is topped by a golden statue of Victoria and has a viewing platform.

name: East Side Gallery
short_description: The East Side Gallery is the longest remaining section of the Berlin Wall, about 1.3 kilometres long, painted by 118 artists in 1990.

name: Hackescher Markt
short_description: Hackescher Markt is a lively area with restaurants, shops and the Hackesche Höfe, a group of connected courtyards.

name: Charlottenburg Palace (Schloss Charlottenburg)
short_description: Charlottenburg Palace (Schloss Charlottenburg) is the largest palace in Berlin, a baroque palace with large gardens, built at the end of the 17th century.

name: Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church (Kaiser-Wilhelm-Gedächtniskirche)
short_description: The Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church was badly damaged in the Second World War; its ruined tower was kept as a memorial against war, next to a modern church from the 1960s.

name: Tempelhofer Feld
short_description: Tempelhofer Feld is a former airport turned into a huge public park, where people walk, cycle and skate on the old runways.

name: Berlin Wall Memorial (Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer)
short_description: The Berlin Wall Memorial on Bernauer Straße is the central memorial of the Berlin Wall, with a preserved section of the border strip and a viewing tower.

name: Oberbaum Bridge (Oberbaumbrücke)
short_description: The Oberbaum Bridge (Oberbaumbrücke) is a red-brick double-deck bridge over the Spree that connects Kreuzberg and Friedrichshain and was a border crossing during the Cold War.

name: Kurfürstendamm
short_description: Kurfürstendamm, known as the 'Ku'damm', is the most famous shopping boulevard of the former West Berlin.

name: KaDeWe
short_description: KaDeWe is one of the largest department stores in Europe, opened in 1907 and famous for its food hall on the sixth floor.

name: Jewish Museum Berlin (Jüdisches Museum)
short_description: The Jewish Museum Berlin (Jüdisches Museum) presents Jewish history in Germany and is known for its zigzag building designed by Daniel Libeskind.

name: Soviet War Memorial in Treptower Park (Sowjetisches Ehrenmal)
short_description: The Soviet War Memorial in Treptower Park is a huge memorial and military cemetery for Soviet soldiers who died in the Battle of Berlin in 1945, with a 12-metre statue of a soldier holding a child.

name: DDR Museum
short_description: The DDR Museum is an interactive museum about everyday life in the German Democratic Republic (East Germany).

name: Unter den Linden
short_description: Unter den Linden is Berlin's historic boulevard, named after its linden trees, running from the Brandenburg Gate to Museum Island.

name: Mauerpark
short_description: Mauerpark is a park on the former death strip of the Berlin Wall, famous for its Sunday flea market and open-air karaoke.

name: Berlin Zoo (Zoologischer Garten)
short_description: The Berlin Zoo (Zoologischer Garten) opened in 1844 and is the oldest zoo in Germany.

name: Teufelsberg
short_description: Teufelsberg is an artificial hill made of war rubble, with a former US listening station from the Cold War and views over the city.

name: Sanssouci Palace (Schloss Sanssouci)
short_description: Sanssouci Palace (Schloss Sanssouci) was the summer palace of Frederick the Great in Potsdam, a UNESCO World Heritage Site less than one hour by train from Berlin.
